text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Region-eu-west latency SLO breach detected (p99 streaming stalls). Auto-paging on-call. Impact: streaming tail stalls, TLS handshake spikes, intermittent DNS failures for cross-zone NAT flows. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/alerts/1769805123 :rotating_light:

jessica: on it. seeing p95 ~ 600ms, p99 > 3.2s for streaming endpoints in eu-west-1 -> eu-west-2 cross-zone flows. customers with dedicated pools seeing increased tail latency. paging network + infra.

leo: ack. pulling tcpdump and natgw metrics. initial signs of SNAT port exhaustion on nat-02 in eu-west-1a around 09:02UTC. also seeing 5xx TLS handshake timeouts.

maria: i see elevated packet loss between AZs, and dns resolution latencies up too. could be route table churn, or a problem with cross-AZ ENI path. starting traceroutes to nat-02 and gateway IPs.

sam: support reports 7 customer incidents flagged as streaming stalls, 3 are high-priority. forwarding ticket ids: TKT-4234, TKT-4237, TKT-4241. customers report stall at token ~1200 and permanent stream close.

jessica: quick triage checklist: 1) freeze rollouts 2) fail traffic to same-AZ where possible 3) check natgw metrics (SNAT ports, connection tracking) 4) enable fallback model routing if backend model timeouts 

katie: adding playbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/network-nat-snat-playbook

leo: dump of natgw stats (snippet):
```
# metric snapshot
natgw:nat-02: connections = 978321
natgw:nat-02: ephemeral_ports_used = 65230 / 65535
natgw:nat-02: conn_fail_tls = 431
```

leo: also ran `kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -o wide` — no large restarts but a few pods in eu-west-2 show longer initial connect times.

maria: traceroute output (shortened):
```
1 10.0.1.1 (10.0.1.1) 0.45 ms
2 10.0.5.10 (10.0.5.10) 4.12 ms
3 100.64.0.5 (100.64.0.5) 120.8 ms  <-- cross-AZ hop elevated
4 100.64.0.6 (100.64.0.6) 2.13 ms
```

maria: that 120ms hop is suspicious. correlates with p99 jumps. filing a ticket with cloud-provider network ops now.

jessica: mitigation plan (short):
- temporarily route traffic to same-AZ model pools for latency-sensitive routes (apply route policy in router service)
- spin up a per-AZ NAT gateway to avoid SNAT port sharing across AZs
- reduce keepalive reuse to lower ephemeral port pressure
- add short-term client-side retry/backoff for streaming chunk fetches

sam: informing affected customers w/ status update. Draft note: 'we are investigating cross-AZ network latency causing streaming stalls; mitigating by routing to same-AZ and adding NAT capacity. ETA 30-45m for visible improvement.'

leo: executing command to provision NAT in eu-west-1b and attach route table rule (devops-run):
```
aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id subnet-0b1234 --allocation-id eipalloc-0a1b2c
# then update route table id rtb-0e9f to point 10.0.0.0/16 -> natgw-new
```

jessica: rolling policy to route sticky clients to same-AZ done. applying on the router service now. watch logs for reduced cross-zone flows.

katie: observability update: after sticky routing started at 09:12UTC p99 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.1s in eu-west-1 within 6m for streaming endpoints. p95 stable ~ 350-420ms. customer tickets still showing some residual stalls.

maria: cloud provider responded: transient fabric congestion affecting cross-AZ path in eu-west region, they are remediating. recommended we avoid amplification of cross-AZ flows until their fix propagates.

leo: NAT gateway created and attached. ephemeral ports usage now distributed; nat-02 ports down to 22k used. TLS handshake errors dropped by ~78%.

jessica: great. next step: keep sticky routing for 2hr, monitor, then slowly relax. leave dedicated customers pinned to local-AZ pool for 24h.

sam: customer update posted to TKT-4234/4237/4241. customers acknowledged.

priya: taking over on-call at 09:25UTC. summary for handoff: cross-AZ network congestion caused NAT SNAT pressure + tls handshake timeouts leading to streaming tail stalls and p99 SLO breach. mitigations applied: per-AZ NAT, sticky same-AZ routing, cloud provider mitigation in progress. key metrics: p99 from 3.2s -> 1.1s; nat ephemeral port usage redistributed. watchlist: dns spikes, any return of cross-AZ flows.

jessica: handoff notes added to incident doc. tagging postmortem owner katie. please escalate if any customer regressions. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident status changed to 'mitigated' at 09:30UTC. creating incident channel and postmortem checklist.

priya: will keep monitoring for next 6 hours and follow up with postmortem draft. thanks team.
